clue.text: One reluctant to join party with a large liberal elite

parts.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
the flower of a group is its elite

explanation.surface: A liberal elite at a big party, and somebody who would rather not join in.
explanation.walkthrough: "Party" here is a social gathering, not a political one, despite "liberal elite" pulling towards politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower hangs back at a dance or party rather than joining in.

clue.text: The Killers or Stock, Aitken and Waterman, say

definitions.meaning: contract killers, paid to carry out a hit
a trio of men who produced a string of chart hits

explanation.surface: A list of pop acts: the American band The Killers and the 1980s British hit-making production team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Killers are a rock band, so both halves look like pop trivia. Stock, Aitken and Waterman were a British trio who produced dozens of chart hits in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Killers-for-hire are hitmen, and men who churn out hits are, punningly, hit men.

clue.text: A part of working? That's being cool-headed!

indicators.note: cool is put at the head, before working

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone asking what part of a job needs, and answering: keeping a cool head.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cool-headed" reads as calm, but it is an instruction: cool (IN) heads working (ON).
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: being party to a secret or scheme is being a part of it.

clue.text: Steal vehicle close to detective, but be cautious

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A car thief being warned to watch out for the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the verb phrase "be cautious"; "but" only joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: telling someone to watch out is telling them to be cautious.

clue.text: More drugs that heartless lags will inject

indicators.note: the heart of LAGS (AG) is removed

parts.note: E = ecstasy, twice for plural drugs
LAGS without its middle AG, placed between the two Es

explanation.surface: Prisoners injecting still more drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the lags injecting; the wordplay reverses it, with the drugs taking in the lags.
explanation.definitionFit: "Anything else?" means "anything more?"

clue.text: Out-of-head member of your clan in high spirits

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is taken out

parts.note: RELATION, a member of your family, without its first letter R

explanation.surface: A relative who is out of their head and very merry.
explanation.walkthrough: "Out-of-head" suggests someone drunk or high; it is a beheading instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: great joy and excitement amount to high spirits.

clue.text: A place a stud might go around, getting disease

indicators.note: the letters go round, turning back to front

parts.note: an earlobe, where a stud earring goes

explanation.surface: Someone's piercing turning into an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: A + LOBE turned round gives the answer; "go around" sounds like the stud going through the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a deadly haemorrhagic fever from central Africa is a disease.

clue.text: Improvise brief defence to secure chess file

indicators.note: cut short, losing its last letter
to secure something is to hold it fast

parts.note: chessboard files are lettered a to h; the d-file is one

explanation.surface: A chess player thinking on their feet to protect a file.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, a file is a column of the board, named by a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin ad libitum, 'at pleasure': to speak without a script.

clue.text: Knight in boozer with single noblewoman in Paris

parts.note: a boozer is a pub, a bar

indicators.note: the knight goes in the single

parts.note: one = single; N goes inside to make ONNE

explanation.surface: A knight drinking in a pub with an unmarried French aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: "In Paris" flags a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign-language equivalent: the French feminine of baron, signalled by 'in Paris'.

clue.text: Lie about spondulicks, not having any yen

parts.note: spondulicks and lolly are both British slang for money
Y = yen, the Japanese currency; removed from LOLLY

explanation.surface: Someone lying about money, claiming to have no longing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: "Yen" also means a longing, so the surface reads as someone lying about not wanting money.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lounge or sprawl lazily is to lie about.

clue.text: Moon regent travelling around country abroad

indicators.note: letters that travel around do not stay in their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruler named Moon on a foreign tour.
explanation.walkthrough: "Moon" looks like a name, but its letters join REGENT to make the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Montenegro is a Balkan country, abroad from a British solver's point of view.

clue.text: Naughty boys seizing northern infertile region

explanation.surface: Delinquents taking over a barren stretch of the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad lads is British slang for tearaways or troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Badlands are barren, eroded land where little grows.

clue.text: Down? Flipping take too many drugs, Hoskins?

definitions.note: Hoskins is the setter, mocking himself; the question mark flags the definition by example.

explanation.surface: A mock-despairing question about whether the setter is depressed and overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: "Flipping" reads as a mild British swearword; it is a reversal instruction. A saddo is British slang for a pathetic, boring person.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter jokingly calls himself a saddo, a pathetic loser.

clue.text: Laurel found in outskirts of Armenia's capital

indicators.note: to be found in a place is to be inside it
just the outer letters are used

parts.note: first and last letters of ArmeniA
Stan Laurel, of Laurel and Hardy; goes between the two As

explanation.surface: A laurel tree growing on the edge of Yerevan.
explanation.walkthrough: "Armenia's capital" suggests Yerevan, but the capital is Kazakhstan's; Armenia only supplies its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the seat of government of Kazakhstan is a capital city.

clue.text: Actor in rug belted about in comfortable motor

indicators.note: bashed around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor in a toupee being beaten up in a plush car.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rug" is slang for a wig, which makes the surface comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring car is a roomy car built for long, comfortable journeys.

clue.text: Once again understood leader must become adult

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: A = adult (film rating); replaces the K

explanation.surface: Someone learning afresh that the boss has to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader of KNEW is its first letter, which must become A.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: afresh, starting over, means once again.

clue.text: Foreign banker once more repelled artist

explanation.surface: An overseas banker driving off a painter a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: A "banker" in crosswords is often a river, something with banks; this one is in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara is a river, a thing with banks, and it lies outside Britain.

clue.text: Confuse Serpent mostly without fail ultimately

indicators.note: most of a word, but not all, so the last letter is dropped
ultimately means in the end, so the end letter of fail is taken

parts.note: ADDER, a snake, minus its last letter
last letter of faiL, placed inside ADDE

explanation.surface: An infallible snake bewildering someone.
explanation.walkthrough: "Without fail" reads as "always", but "without" here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to muddle someone's brain is to confuse them.

clue.text: English queen hugged by American escort is ok

indicators.note: whatever is hugged is held in someone's arms

parts.note: a date escorts you out; EQU goes after its D

explanation.surface: An English queen being cuddled by her American companion, who gets a so-so review.
explanation.walkthrough: QU for queen is a standard abbreviation; "is" only links the wordplay to "ok".
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means ok, good enough.

clue.text: One person exploiting another one taking horse?

definitions.meaning: someone who exploits other people for their own ends
horse is slang for heroin, so this is a drug taker

explanation.surface: Someone taking advantage of another by making off with their horse.
explanation.walkthrough: "Horse" is drug slang for heroin, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is both an exploiter of others and a drug taker.

clue.text: King meets a bishop, one with European girl's name

parts.note: K = king, in chess and cards
RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A king and a bishop meeting someone who has a European girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads "European girl's name" as one phrase; European only supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a spelling of the name Carrie is a girl's name.

clue.text: Golden one in European department's made a minister

indicators.note: one being in something means it sits inside

parts.note: a Dane is a European; I goes inside to make DAINE

explanation.surface: A star member of a European department being given a ministerial post.
explanation.walkthrough: "Minister" suggests government, but a minister is also a member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious sense: being admitted to holy orders is being made a minister.

clue.text: Strip of Dundee requiring some alterations

indicators.note: the letters of DUNDEE need rearranging

explanation.surface: A strip of land in the Scottish city of Dundee needing building work.
explanation.walkthrough: "Strip" reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lay bare, removing every covering, is to strip.

clue.text: One aids evacuation of soldiers up in eastern area

explanation.surface: A military evacuation of troops from an eastern region.
explanation.walkthrough: The evacuation is of the bowels, not of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema helps empty the bowels.

clue.text: I am a gruff bleeding northern guttersnipe

indicators.note: damaged, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rough street kid from the north introducing himself with a swearword.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bleeding" is a mild British swearword, which disguises it as an anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy street child, a guttersnipe.

clue.text: Early man found by academician on embankment?

parts.note: DAM, a barrier across a river

explanation.surface: A caveman discovered by a scholar on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, "on" puts A above DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Bible's first human is the earliest man of all.

clue.text: Pretty-looking female with wind

explanation.surface: An attractive woman with flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's wind is the bodily kind; the wordplay wants plain moving air.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means beautiful, pretty to look at.

clue.text: Passes work with eager singletons primarily

parts.note: to work, of a machine, is to go

indicators.note: only the first letters are used

explanation.surface: A dating-app job that keeps keen single people busy.
explanation.walkthrough: Singletons are single people; only their first letter joins with that of eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: time that elapses passes, or moves on.

clue.text: Flipping Dada paintings in a class of their own?

definitions.text: in a class of their own

parts.note: dada and pa both mean father

explanation.surface: Dadaist paintings praised as unique.
explanation.walkthrough: Dada was an art movement, which the surface leans on; here it is a child's word for father.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something set aside from all others is in a class of its own.

clue.text: Hot articles Hoskins had knocked over in state

indicators.note: turned over, so ANAID reads DIANA

parts.note: the setter refers to himself: I

explanation.surface: The setter having knocked over some hot items somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so Hoskins gives I; "had" gives D as in I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a Midwestern US state.
